benefits.name: Energy Assistance Payment
benefits.provider: WA Government (via Synergy or Horizon Power)
benefits.summary: A yearly credit on your electricity bill, paid in daily amounts, if you hold a concession card.
benefits.eligibility_text: Residential electricity account holder with a Pensioner Concession Card (Centrelink or DVA), Health Care Card or DVA Gold Card. Horizon Power and the ECES also list the Commonwealth Seniors Health Card.
benefits.value_text: $377.14 a year credited to your electricity account
benefits.how_to_claim: Add your concession card in your Synergy or Horizon Power online account, or phone your retailer.
benefits.notes: Synergy's page still shows $334.49 (older year) and does not list CSHC; Horizon Power and RevenueWA ECES pages show $377.14 from 1 July 2026 and include CSHC. Check CSHC eligibility with Synergy. Replaced the old Cost of Living Assistance payment.

benefits.name: Air Conditioning Rebate
benefits.provider: WA Government (via Synergy or Horizon Power)
benefits.summary: Help with air-conditioner running costs for seniors living in the hot north of WA.
benefits.eligibility_text: Live north of the 26th parallel and/or the 50 Day Relative Strain Index line, and hold a WA Seniors Card plus a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card, Pensioner Concession Card or DVA Pensioner Concession Card (both cards needed). Families with dependent children on a concession card also qualify. Air conditioner must be installed at the home.
benefits.value_text: $78.98 for each eligible month (cost of 221.8 kWh); 2 to 10 eligible months depending on town
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply online through Synergy or Horizon Power with your bill and card details.
benefits.notes: Needs BOTH a WA Seniors Card and one of PCC/CSHC/DVA PCC for seniors. Max per year = $78.98 x eligible months for your town (up to about $790). Synergy page shows older $70.05/month example.

benefits.name: Account Establishment Fee Rebate
benefits.provider: WA Government (via Synergy or Horizon Power)
benefits.summary: One-off refund of the fee to open a new electricity account.
benefits.eligibility_text: Residential customer opening a new electricity account with a Health Care Card, Pensioner Concession Card, DVA Gold Card or DVA Pensioner Concession Card.
benefits.value_text: One-off $27.28 (Horizon Power) / $26.84 (Synergy) on your first bill
benefits.value_period: 2026-27 (Horizon); Synergy figure may be older year
benefits.how_to_claim: Tell your retailer you hold a concession card when you open the account.
benefits.notes: One-off, so max_annual_value null.

benefits.name: Reduced Meter Test Fee
benefits.summary: A cheaper fee if you ask for your electricity meter to be tested, refunded if the meter is faulty.
benefits.eligibility_text: Holders of a Centrelink Health Care Card, Pensioner Concession Card, DVA Gold Card or DVA Pensioner Concession Card.
benefits.value_text: Reduced meter test fee (amount not stated); fee refunded if meter is faulty
benefits.how_to_claim: Ask your electricity retailer for a meter test and give your concession card details.
benefits.notes: Fee amount not shown on source.

benefits.name: Energy Concession Extension Scheme (ECES)
benefits.summary: Gets you the Energy Assistance Payment if you pay for power through a caravan park, retirement village or other landlord/on-seller instead of Synergy or Horizon Power.
benefits.eligibility_text: You pay for electricity through an eligible on-selling arrangement (e.g. retirement village, caravan park, other retailer such as Perth Energy or Alinta) and you or a household member hold a PCC, HCC, CSHC or DVA Gold Card. WA Seniors Card alone does not qualify. Tenants must have lived there or have a lease of at least 3 months.
benefits.value_text: Energy Assistance Payment $377.14 a year paid by EFT (plus Air Conditioning Rebate if eligible)
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply online via RevenueWAConnect Online Services Portal; renew yearly by your anniversary date.

benefits.name: Life Support Equipment Energy Subsidy
benefits.summary: A yearly payment to help with the power costs of running life support equipment at home.
benefits.eligibility_text: Patient (or their guardian/carer) depends on specified life support equipment at home on specialist advice, and holds a Pensioner Concession Card (Centrelink or DVA), Health Care Card (not CSHC) or Health Care Interim Voucher.
benefits.value_text: From $58 (nebuliser) to $1,517 (child oxygen concentrator) a year depending on equipment; e.g. CPAP $530, adult oxygen concentrator $1,011
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply online through RevenueWAConnect; your doctor completes the medical authorisation. Renew yearly.
benefits.notes: Max shown is the highest item rate (child oxygen concentrator); most adults get less. CSHC is excluded.

benefits.name: Thermoregulatory Dysfunction Energy Subsidy
benefits.summary: A yearly payment for people whose medical condition means they must heat or cool their home.
benefits.eligibility_text: Patient (or guardian/carer in the same household) holds a Pensioner Concession Card, Health Care Card (not CSHC) or Health Care Interim Voucher; patient meets at least two of three qualifying conditions, certified by a doctor who has treated them for 3+ months.
benefits.value_text: $832 a year paid in advance (up to two payments per household)
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply online through RevenueWAConnect; your doctor completes the medical form. Renew yearly.

benefits.name: Hardship Utility Grant Scheme (HUGS)
benefits.provider: Department of Communities (via your utility provider)
benefits.summary: A grant to help pay an overdue electricity, gas or water bill if you are in financial hardship.
benefits.eligibility_text: Assessed by your utility provider as being in financial hardship, completed a payment arrangement of at least 90 days, and still owe more than $300. Must live at the supply address. Water customers must be owner-occupiers. Not for bottled gas.
benefits.value_text: Up to $640 a year (south of the 26th parallel) or $1,060 (Denham and north), max 85% of the balance
benefits.how_to_claim: Call your utility provider, join their hardship program, then ask them to start a HUGS application after 90 days.
benefits.notes: Max $1,060 applies only in the north; $640 south.

benefits.name: Local Government Rates Rebate (pensioners, and Seniors Card plus CSHC)
benefits.provider: Water Corporation / RevenueWA (applied by your council)
benefits.summary: Up to half off your council rates if you own and live in your home.
benefits.eligibility_text: Own and live in the property as your main home and hold a Pensioner Concession Card or State Concession Card, OR hold BOTH a WA Seniors Card and a Commonwealth Seniors Health Card. Includes long-term (5+ year) leases in retirement villages, lifestyle villages, park homes and caravan parks. DVA Gold Card holders may qualify via the State Concession Card.
benefits.value_text: Up to 50% off council rates, capped at $750 a year
benefits.value_period: Rating year 1 July to 30 June (fact sheet as at July 2026)
benefits.how_to_claim: Register once via Water Corporation's online concession form; it tells your council. Pay the balance by 30 June to keep the rebate.
benefits.notes: Seniors Card + CSHC need BOTH cards; DVA_GOLD only through a State Concession Card (selected TPI/EDA/war widow categories).

benefits.name: Local Government Rates Rebate (WA Seniors Card only)
benefits.provider: Water Corporation / RevenueWA (applied by your council)
benefits.summary: A smaller discount on council rates for WA Seniors Card holders who own and live in their home.
benefits.eligibility_text: Own and live in the property as your main home and hold a WA Seniors Card (without a CSHC or PCC).
benefits.value_text: Up to 25% off council rates, capped at $100 a year
benefits.value_period: Rating year 1 July to 30 June (fact sheet as at July 2026)
benefits.how_to_claim: Register via Water Corporation's online concession form; pay the balance by 30 June.
benefits.notes: No deferral option for Seniors Card only.

benefits.name: Rates and water charges deferral
benefits.summary: Pensioners can put off paying council rates, ESL and water charges, interest-free, until the home is sold.
benefits.eligibility_text: Registered for the pensioner rebate with a PCC or State Concession Card, or with BOTH a WA Seniors Card and CSHC. Seniors Card alone cannot defer.
benefits.value_text: Defer unpaid rates, ESL and water charges with no interest; repaid when you sell, move or on death (unless a surviving partner stays)
benefits.how_to_claim: Charges are deferred automatically if unpaid by 30 June once you are registered.
benefits.notes: Cannot claim the rebate on amounts that are deferred.

benefits.name: Emergency Services Levy Rebate
benefits.summary: The same pensioner or seniors discount you get on council rates also applies to the Emergency Services Levy.
benefits.eligibility_text: Registered for the council rates rebate: PCC or State Concession Card, or WA Seniors Card plus CSHC (up to 50%); WA Seniors Card only (up to 25%).
benefits.value_text: Up to 50% off the ESL (pensioners, Seniors + CSHC) or up to 25% (Seniors Card only)
benefits.how_to_claim: Applied automatically once registered for the rates rebate.
benefits.notes: No dollar cap stated for ESL.

benefits.name: Underground Electricity Connection Charge Rebate
benefits.summary: A discount on the council charge for connecting your home to underground power.
benefits.eligibility_text: Owner-occupier registered for the pensioners and seniors rebate.
benefits.value_text: Up to 50% off (PCC, State Concession Card, or Seniors Card + CSHC); Seniors Card only up to 25%, capped at $100, first year only
benefits.how_to_claim: Applied once registered for the rates rebate; ask your council.
benefits.notes: One-off charge so no annual value.

benefits.name: Water Corporation service charge rebate (pensioners, and Seniors Card plus CSHC)
benefits.summary: Up to half off the fixed water, sewerage and drainage charges on your Water Corporation bill.
benefits.eligibility_text: Main residence; Pensioner Concession Card or State Concession Card, OR both a WA Seniors Card and CSHC (CSHC alone not eligible).
benefits.value_text: Up to 50% off service charges, capped at $600 a year (water $108.86, sewerage $436.15, drainage $54.99)
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply online with Water Corporation's concession form; reapply if you move or get a new card.
benefits.notes: Interest is not charged on overdue bills for these cardholders.

benefits.name: Water Corporation water use rebate (pensioners)
benefits.summary: Half off the cost of the first block of water you use each year, for pensioners including renters.
benefits.eligibility_text: Pensioner Concession Card or State Concession Card holders. Tenants qualify if they do not live with the owner. Seniors Card + CSHC holders do not get this part.
benefits.value_text: 50% off the first 150 kL in Perth (max $158.10), first 400 kL south country, first 600 kL north country (max depends on town, e.g. $891.28)
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply online with Water Corporation's concession form.
benefits.notes: Country maximums are higher and vary by town class; $158.10 is the metro cap.

benefits.name: Water Corporation service charge rebate (WA Seniors Card only)
benefits.summary: Up to $100 off fixed water charges for WA Seniors Card holders.
benefits.eligibility_text: WA Seniors Card holder (without a PCC or CSHC), main residence.
benefits.value_text: Up to $100 a year off service charges
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply online with Water Corporation's concession form.

benefits.name: Busselton Water pensioner and seniors rebate
benefits.summary: Discount on Busselton Water bills for pensioners and seniors who own their home.
benefits.eligibility_text: Own and live in the property (incl. long-term retirement village / park home leases). PCC, CSHC or State Concession Card: up to 50%; WA Seniors Card: up to 25% off supply charge only.
benefits.value_text: Up to 50% off supply charge and first 350 kL of water (PCC, CSHC, State Concession Card); up to 25% off supply charge (Seniors Card)
benefits.how_to_claim: Download the form and return it to Busselton Water with a copy of your card.
benefits.notes: Busselton area only. No cap or phone number on page. Page lists CSHC alone, unlike Water Corporation.

benefits.name: Aqwest (Bunbury) water concession
benefits.summary: Discount on Bunbury water bills for pensioners and seniors.
benefits.eligibility_text: Valid PCC, State Concession Card or WA Seniors Card (with or without CSHC). Owner-occupiers, retirement village residents, and tenants with a Pensioner or Seniors card. HCC and DVA Gold alone not eligible.
benefits.value_text: Discount on water charges (percentage not stated on page)
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply online or with the PDF form; tenants with the account in landlord's name must apply by 31 July each year.
benefits.notes: Bunbury area only. DVA_GOLD only via State Concession Card.

benefits.name: State Concession Card
benefits.summary: A WA card that gives certain DVA Gold Card holders the same rates and water rebates as pensioners.
benefits.eligibility_text: DVA Gold Card holders without a PCC who are TPI, TTI, EDA, SRDP, war widows/widowers, blinded war pensioners, or other listed DVA categories.
benefits.value_text: Access to pensioner rebates on council rates, water service and water use charges
benefits.how_to_claim: Download and send the State Concession Card application form.

benefits.name: WA Seniors Card
benefits.provider: Department of Communities (WA Seniors Card Centre)
benefits.summary: Free card for WA seniors 65+ that unlocks free off-peak public transport, rebates and business discounts.
benefits.eligibility_text: Aged 65 or over, Australian citizen or permanent resident, living in WA, and retired or working no more than 25 hours a week.
benefits.value_text: Free card; access to Cost of Living Rebate, free Transperth off-peak travel, rates/water rebates and discounts
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply online at seniorscard.wa.gov.au.

benefits.name: Cost of Living Rebate (WA Seniors Card)
benefits.provider: Department of Communities (WA Seniors Card Centre)
benefits.summary: A yearly cash payment into your bank account for registered WA Seniors Card members.
benefits.eligibility_text: Registered WA Seniors Card member; new applicants must be received by 31 May for that year's payment.
benefits.value_text: $114.20 single, $171.30 couple
benefits.how_to_claim: Register your bank details with the WA Seniors Card Centre by 31 May; no need to reapply each year.
benefits.notes: $171.30 is per couple; single max $114.20.

benefits.name: Safety and Security Rebate
benefits.provider: Department of Communities (WA Seniors Card Centre)
benefits.summary: Get back up to $400 for buying home security or safety items like alarms, screens, deadlocks or smoke alarms.
benefits.eligibility_text: WA Seniors Card member at the time of purchase; item installed at your principal WA home. Not for aged care, hospital or hostel residents. One claim per household.
benefits.value_text: One-off rebate up to $400 for eligible items bought on or after 22 Aug 2021
benefits.value_period: Ongoing since 22 Aug 2021 (no end date set)
benefits.how_to_claim: Buy and install the item, then apply online or by form with tax receipts and ID.
benefits.notes: One-off ($400 lifetime per household) so max_annual_value null.

benefits.name: Transperth free off-peak travel (Seniors SmartRider)
benefits.summary: Free bus, train and ferry travel in Perth at off-peak times and weekends for WA Seniors Card holders.
benefits.eligibility_text: WA Seniors Card holder using a Seniors SmartRider.
benefits.value_text: Free 9am to 3:30pm and 7pm to 6am weekdays, all weekend, public holidays and Seniors Week; concession fares at other times
benefits.how_to_claim: Get a Seniors SmartRider linked to your WA Seniors Card.
benefits.notes: Phone 13 62 13 is Transperth's InfoLine (not on source page; verify).

benefits.name: Transperth Pensioner and Veteran SmartRider
benefits.summary: Concession fares and free travel on Perth public transport for age pensioners, carers and veterans.
benefits.eligibility_text: Aged pensioners and carers (Pensioner SmartRider), veterans/war widows (Veteran SmartRider). HCC holders get concession fares only.
benefits.value_text: Concession fare or free travel (times not stated on page)
benefits.how_to_claim: Get a Pensioner or Veteran SmartRider.
benefits.notes: Free travel times not stated on the Transperth page; HCC is concession fare only.

benefits.name: Transwa regional coach and rail concession
benefits.summary: Half-price regional train and coach fares across WA.
benefits.eligibility_text: Pensioner Concession Card, State-issued Seniors card or Seniors SmartRider, Veteran SmartRider, DVA PCC or Gold Card. CSHC alone does not qualify.
benefits.value_text: 50% off the regular fare
benefits.how_to_claim: Book online (registered cardholders) or by phone/booking centre.

benefits.name: Transwa Pensioner Free Travel
benefits.summary: Free regional train or coach trips each year for WA pensioners and DVA Gold Card holders.
benefits.eligibility_text: WA Pensioner Concession Card (Services Australia or DVA) holders, and WA DVA Gold Card holders.
benefits.value_text: 2 free single trips a year (PCC) or 4 (DVA Gold), plus 50% off other fares
benefits.how_to_claim: Register online, by phone, post or at a booking centre (up to 10 business days).
benefits.notes: Dollar value depends on route.

benefits.name: Regional Pensioner Travel Card
benefits.summary: A card loaded with a set amount each year for fuel or taxis, for pensioners living in regional WA.
benefits.eligibility_text: Receiving a means-tested pension (Age Pension, Carer Payment, DSP, DVA Service Pension, Income Support Supplement) and living in an eligible regional location.
benefits.value_text: Set amount each year for fuel and/or taxis (amount not stated on page)
benefits.how_to_claim: Get the form from a participating Australia Post office and submit by 15 May for the coming financial year.
benefits.notes: Replaces the Country Age Pension Fuel Card. Annual dollar amount not on source. From 1 Oct 2026 fuel retailers may surcharge.

benefits.name: Vehicle licence (registration) concession
benefits.summary: Half off the vehicle licence fee on one car for pensioners and Seniors Card plus CSHC holders.
benefits.eligibility_text: Pensioner Concession Card (Centrelink or DVA), or BOTH a WA Seniors Card and CSHC. One vehicle only (car, light goods under 3t, motorhome, motorcycle). 100% for certain veterans (TPI/EDA/SRDP) and max-rate DSP/carer/blind pensioners.
benefits.value_text: 50% off the vehicle licence fee (100% for some veterans and disability pensioners)
benefits.how_to_claim: Fill in the C1 Application for concession form and show your card(s).
benefits.notes: Phone from WA Seniors Card benefits page.

benefits.name: Driver's licence fee concession
benefits.summary: Free or half-price driver's licence renewal for pensioners and seniors.
benefits.eligibility_text: 100% free: PCC holders on the Age Pension, or WA Seniors Card + CSHC, or DVA Gold TPI/EDA/SRDP. 50% off: PCC (Centrelink or DVA) or WA Seniors Card.
benefits.value_text: 100% or 50% off licence renewal/replacement fees
benefits.how_to_claim: Show your card(s) when renewing; use the C1 form. Refunds may apply if you paid full fees while eligible.

benefits.name: WA Photo Card fee concession
benefits.summary: Free or half-price WA Photo Card (ID card) for pensioners and seniors.
benefits.eligibility_text: Same rules as driver's licence: free for Age Pension PCC holders or Seniors Card + CSHC; 50% off for PCC or Seniors Card.
benefits.value_text: 100% or 50% off Photo Card fee
benefits.how_to_claim: Show your card(s) when applying.

benefits.name: Recreational fishing licence discount
benefits.summary: Half-price recreational fishing licences for WA Seniors Card holders.
benefits.eligibility_text: WA Seniors Card holders (other concession cards may also qualify; DPIRD page's concession section did not load).
benefits.value_text: 50% off recreational fishing licences (standard fees $40-$50)
benefits.how_to_claim: Buy your licence online through DPIRD and select the concession.
benefits.notes: Concession detail missing on DPIRD page; PCC eligibility not confirmed.

benefits.name: Ambulance fee subsidy (St John WA)
benefits.provider: WA Department of Health / St John WA
benefits.summary: Free ambulance for over-65 pensioners, and half price for other over-65s or under-65 pensioners.
benefits.eligibility_text: WA residents over 65 with a pension concession entitlement: free. Over 65 without one, or under 65 with one: pay 50%. Service must be medically necessary.
benefits.value_text: Free (65+ with pension concession) or 50% off ambulance fees
benefits.how_to_claim: Contact St John's Finance Customer Team about your bill.
benefits.notes: Applies with no card if aged 65+ (50%); use aged_65 logic manually. Page only says 'Pension Concession Entitlement'.

benefits.name: Public dental care for adults
benefits.summary: Subsidised general and emergency dental care at public clinics for concession card holders.
benefits.eligibility_text: Aged 17+ with a current Health Care Card or Pensioner Concession Card. Includes the Country and Metropolitan Patients Dental Subsidy Schemes (private dentists).
benefits.value_text: Subsidised dental care (co-payment not stated)
benefits.how_to_claim: Phone Dental Health Services to get on the waiting list.
benefits.notes: Patient co-payment amounts not on page.

benefits.name: Spectacle Subsidy Scheme
benefits.summary: Up to $54.34 every two years towards glasses or contact lenses.
benefits.eligibility_text: Receive an Age, Disability or Service pension, or hold a WA Seniors Card. DVA Gold Card holders not eligible.
benefits.value_text: Up to $54.34 every 2 years
benefits.how_to_claim: Ask your optometrist for the claim form when you buy your glasses.
benefits.notes: Paid every 2 years so max_annual_value null (about $27/yr).

benefits.name: Patient Assisted Travel Scheme (PATS)
benefits.summary: Helps country people with travel and accommodation costs to reach specialist treatment far from home.
benefits.eligibility_text: Country WA residents travelling over 100 km (70-100 km for cancer/renal) to the nearest eligible specialist service, assessed under the PATS Handbook. From 1 July 2026 also covers approved specialist allied health and dental.
benefits.value_text: 40c per km fuel; accommodation $20/night private or up to $110/night commercial (+$15 support person); $20 per return trip for 70-100 km cancer/renal
benefits.how_to_claim: Get your specialist/GP to sign the PATS form and lodge it with your local PATS office.
benefits.notes: No card needed; phone via local PATS office.

benefits.name: Community Aids and Equipment Program (CAEP)
benefits.summary: Equipment like wheelchairs and home changes like ramps for people with long-term or age-related impairment living at home.
benefits.eligibility_text: People living at home with long-term health conditions, disability or age-related functional impairment, assessed by a health professional.
benefits.value_text: Equipment and home modifications (cost to client not stated)
benefits.how_to_claim: Ask your GP or allied health professional to complete the CAEP Referral Form.
benefits.notes: Card/income criteria not on page.

benefits.name: Dog and cat registration discount
benefits.summary: Cheaper dog and cat registration for concession card holders.
benefits.eligibility_text: Dog: Pensioner Concession Card holders. Cat: accepted concession card holders.
benefits.value_text: Discounted registration (amount not stated)
benefits.how_to_claim: Show your card when registering your pet with your council.
benefits.notes: Level is State law applied by councils.

benefits.name: Public Trustee will drafting discount
benefits.summary: A cheaper fee to have the Public Trustee write your will if you hold a concession card.
benefits.eligibility_text: Valid concession card holders (exact cards not stated on master list).
benefits.value_text: Discounted will drafting fee (amount not stated)
benefits.how_to_claim: Contact the Public Trustee to book a will appointment.
benefits.notes: Eligible cards to confirm on Public Trustee page.

benefits.name: Attractions and parks concessions
benefits.summary: Discounted entry to Perth Zoo, WA Museum, national parks, Rottnest Island and other state attractions.
benefits.eligibility_text: Concession card holders; WA Seniors Card holders get discounts at the Art Gallery of WA, WA Museum, Perth Zoo, national parks and Rottnest accommodation.
benefits.value_text: Discounted entry (varies by venue)
benefits.how_to_claim: Show your card at the venue or when booking.
benefits.notes: Bundled record; individual prices not loaded.

benefits.name: Land tax concession for veterans' surviving partners
benefits.summary: Lower land tax for eligible war widows, war widowers and widowed mothers of veterans.
benefits.eligibility_text: Eligible war widows, war widowers or veterans' widowed mothers.
benefits.value_text: Reduced assessable land value (amount not stated)
benefits.how_to_claim: Apply for a land tax exemption with RevenueWA.
benefits.notes: Only matters if land tax applies (most owner-occupied homes are already exempt).
